title: pureGAM: Learning an Inherently Pure Additive Model

problem.claim: Generalized Additive Models increasingly include pairwise or higher-order predictor interactions.

gap.claim: Existing models face an identifiability challenge when incorporating such interactions.

contributions.claim: pureGAM is an inherently pure additive model covering main effects and higher-order interactions.
The pureness condition makes pureGAM identifiable without compromising accuracy.
pureGAM provides a unified model for numerical and categorical features with a learning procedure intended to achieve optimal performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose pureGAM as an inherently pure additive model and describe its learning procedure as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that pureGAM outperforms other GAMs and performs competitively against opaque models.
The authors report that pureGAM has stronger interpretability than competitors in terms of pureness.
The authors report successful adoption of pureGAM in one real-world application.

narrative_sequence.summary: GAM research is increasingly incorporating pairwise and higher-order predictor interactions.
Existing interaction-inclusive models have an identifiability challenge.
The paper proposes pureGAM, using a pureness condition for main effects and higher-order interactions.
The pureness condition is reported to preserve accuracy while adding identifiability and simplicity-oriented interpretability.
The authors report broad feature support, competitive evaluations, improved pureness-based interpretability, and one real-world adoption.

unknowns: Evaluation datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are unspecified.
The identifiability proof details and assumptions are unspecified.
The real-world application domain and adoption details are unspecified.
